references.text: God promises to send hornets ahead of the Israelites to drive out the Hivites, Canaanites, and Hittites—the original promise referred to in Deuteronomy 7:20.
Joshua reminds the people that God sent hornets before them to drive out the two Amorite kings—a historical confirmation of the fulfillment of the promise in Deuteronomy 7:20.
Isaiah describes how the Lord will whistle for flies and bees as an instrument of judgment—similar imagery using insects as God's tools.
The following verse explains that God will drive out the nations little by little, not all at once—the context for the gradual destruction mentioned in verse 20.
God promises to put fear and dread of Israel over all peoples under heaven—a thematic parallel to how enemies will be destroyed and forced into hiding.
